units.source: Trilium allows you to save common searches as notes within the note tree. The search results will appear as sub-notes under these "saved search" notes. Here is an example of how it works:

A saved search runs when you open it, and when you expand it in the note tree. A saved search in a tab that is not shown, such as a background tab restored at startup, runs when you switch to that tab. Its results stay until you run the search again with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button of the search parameters. If the query has an error, it appears as a notification.
In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Safe mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__, and when the request fails, the search does not run on its own. Press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Search now__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to run it.

Once a search is saved, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search parameters__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is still available underneath the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Title__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in order to be able to change the settings later on but it will appear collapsed by default.

By default, saved searches are stored in the day note. However, you can designate a different note to store saved searches by marking it with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label. Additionally, for __TRILIUM_PH_1__workspaces__TRILIUM_PH_2__, you can use the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ label to specify a storage location for saved searches within that workspace.
